newsitem.title: ITALY: Police capture alleged Mafia priest-killer.
newsitem.headline: Police capture alleged Mafia priest-killer.

text.p: Police in Sicily claimed another success in their war on the Mafia on Friday with the arrest of an alleged hitman wanted for the killing of a Roman Catholic priest.
Salvatore Grigoli, 42, was captured on Thursday night when police burst into a small apartment on the edge of the Sicilian capital where he had been hiding.

Grigoli, who was preparing a meal when the raid took place, was armed with a pistol but offered no resistance, police said. They said the suspect had grown a goatee beard and sideburns to try to disguise his appearance.

Grigoli had been sought for the slaying in September 1993 of Father Giuseppe Puglisi, who was shot in the back of the head outside his home in the crime-ridden Brancaccio district of Palermo where he preached against the Mafia.

He was also wanted in connection with a failed attempt to kill a prominent Mafia turncoat, Salvatore Contorno, and fatal bomb attacks in Rome, Florence and Milan in 1993 which police have attributed to the Cosa Nostra.
Police have gradually put most of the mob's known bosses behind bars since the bombing murders in 1992 of leading anti-Mafia magistrates Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino.
Their most recent coup was the arrest earlier this month of crime chieftain Pietro Aglieri, a leading lieutenant of captured "boss of bosses" Salvatoren Riina.
